subject: Request: Tiered Escrow Credits + Phased Downgrade Amendment for Helix POC
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily.park@helixhealth.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Ramp / early-termination ask for POC

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers and cost estimates look promising. We're preparing the internal POC sign-off packet and have one ask from procurement: they want an explicit mechanism that protects Helix if our usage ramps slower than projected, and a limited early-termination opt-out in the first 90 days tied to an escrowed credit bucket.

High-level they want:
- A tiered escrow credit equal to 25% of committed spend, released in three tranches (30/60/90 days) if usage ramps to targets.
- If usage is below the 60% ramp target at day 90, Helix can opt to terminate without penalty and receive remaining escrow.
- Clear language so we don't get stranded with long ramp staircases.

Could Redwood consider a short-term amendment to the SOW with this structure? Rajiv (cc) handles procurement — can you advise next steps and whether this requires executive review?

Thanks,
Emily Park
VP, Platform Engineering
Helix Health

Attachments: Helix_SOW_v3.pdf
From: jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com
To: Emily Park <emily.park@helixhealth.com>, Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@helixhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ramp / early-termination ask for POC

Emily / Rajiv — thanks for the clear ask and the SOW. I reviewed the procurement language and sketched a pragmatic amendment that preserves Redwood's economics while giving Helix the comfort you need.

Proposal (summary):
- Escrowed credit pool: 25% of committed quarterly spend held in escrow at contract start.
- Release schedule: 40% at day 30, 30% at day 60, 30% at day 90 contingent on hitting ramp thresholds.
- Ramp thresholds: 40% of projected tokens at D30, 65% at D60, 90% at D90. Missed thresholds permit partial release based on linear interpolation (documented in attached spreadsheet).
- Opt-out clause: If by day 90 Helix has achieved less than 60% of projected consumption, Helix may elect to terminate the POC and receive remaining escrow less any consumed services; no additional early termination fee.

This is intended as a limited-scope amendment for POC only (not a long-term commitment rewrite). I attached a draft ramp schedule and marked the customer-friendly language. If this looks aligned, I need to escalate to Deal Desk + Revenue for signoff on the escrow amount and the interpolation approach.

Next steps:
1) Marissa — looping you in to confirm we can hold 25% as escrow on a POC and signoff approach.
2) Vivek — would like your read on revenue impact and whether we can greenlight the interpolation release policy for this account.
3) Emily/Rajiv — if you can confirm the projected token curve (or an allowance window) I'll finalize the amendment for legal/DocuSign.

Cheers,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: tiered_escrow_and_ramp_schedule.xlsx
From: jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com
To: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: FWD: Request: Tiered Escrow Credits + Phased Downgrade Amendment for Helix POC

Marissa / Vivek — forwarding Helix's ask and my proposed amendment. Quick context: Helix is a strategic POC (national healthcare chain), projected first-quarter commit ~$120k. Procurement insists on a short-term safety net tied to ramp. The model I proposed holds 25% in escrow and releases over 30/60/90 days with a D90 opt-out floor at 60% ramp.

Key deal-desk questions:
- Can Deal Desk approve escrowing 25% of committed spend for a POC without additional collateral?
- Is the interpolation release (partial releases if thresholds partially met) acceptable from revenue recognition / finance perspective?
- Any recommended guardrails (max escrow cap, payout window, reporting cadence)?

I've attached the ramp schedule and a sample amendment clause. We need a quick decision — Helix is targeting an internal exec packet by Friday.

Thanks for the quick review — happy to jump on a 20-min call if helpful.

— Jasmine
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 30 May 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FWD: Request: Tiered Escrow Credits + Phased Downgrade Amendment for Helix POC

Team — reviewed the proposal and the numbers. I support a conditional approval with the following executive guardrails: 

1) Escrow cap: 25% of the quarter's committed spend, not to exceed $35k for any single POC. Finance to confirm journal treatment; escrow held on balance sheet as liability until released/consumed.
2) Release interpolation: acceptable, but releases must be driven by token consumption measured via our ingest logs and audited weekly during the 90-day window.
3) Opt-out floor: maintain the D90 opt-out if consumption <60% — however, Helix forfeits any portion of escrow already released; remaining escrow returned within 10 business days of termination notice.
4) Reporting & dispute window: Helix has 5 business days after each release to dispute consumption numbers; disputes trigger a joint audit window of 10 business days.
5) Legal/Finance signoff required prior to DocuSign: Marissa to coordinate updated amendment and DocuSign flow; Sergio to confirm accounting treatment.

Marissa — please prepare an amendment with the cap and dispute language and route to Legal + Finance for signoff. Jasmine, share the finalized projected token curve from Helix so we can bake exact numbers into the schedule. If all good, I'll authorize the amendment signature.

-Vivek
Chief Revenue Officer
Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
